```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

This file pulls every raw source and saves it to `../data/raw/`. Nothing gets cleaned
here except what is needed to make the next request (for example, pulling the ticker
out of the scraped text so we can look it up at the SEC).

## Settings and packages

```{r settings}
START_YEAR = 2023     # first year of quarterly data we want
REFRESH    = FALSE    # FALSE = reuse files already saved in data/raw (saves time and API money)

raw_dir = "../data/raw"
pr_dir  = file.path(raw_dir, "press_releases")
dir.create(pr_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

pkgs = c("rvest", "httr2", "jsonlite", "dplyr", "tidyr", "purrr", "stringr",
         "readr", "lubridate", "ggplot2", "ellmer", "knitr")
missing_pkgs = pkgs[!pkgs %in% rownames(installed.packages())]
if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) install.packages(missing_pkgs)

library(dplyr)   # only package we attach, everything else uses pkg::function()
```

API keys live in `.Renviron` in the project folder (that file is in `.gitignore`). We need three:

- `SEC_USER_AGENT` - the SEC asks every script to say who it is, e.g. `Your Name your_email@miamioh.edu`
- `FRED_API_KEY`
- `OPENAI_API_KEY`

```{r keys}
# Knitting runs from the markdowns/ folder, so R does not find .Renviron in the project
# folder on its own. Load it directly.
if (file.exists("../.Renviron")) readRenviron("../.Renviron")

needed = c("SEC_USER_AGENT", "FRED_API_KEY", "OPENAI_API_KEY")
have   = Sys.getenv(needed) != ""
if (!all(have)) stop("Add these to .Renviron and restart R: ", paste(needed[!have], collapse = ", "))
```

## Source 1: Nareit REIT Directory (web scraping)

[Nareit's REIT directory](https://www.reit.com/investing/reit-directory) lists every REIT
with its property sector. We filter it to **Retail**, **Public (listed)**, **United States**
using the same query string the site's own filter form builds (`sector=642&status=309&country=2`).
The list is split across pages (`&page=0`, `&page=1`, ...), so we loop until a page comes back empty.

What one row is (list): one retail REIT as shown in the directory table.

```{r nareit-list}
base_url = "https://www.reit.com"
list_url = paste0(base_url, "/investing/reit-directory?company=&sector=642&status=309&country=2&page=")

scrape_list_page = function(p) {
  Sys.sleep(1)  # be polite to the site
  pg   = rvest::read_html(paste0(list_url, p))
  rows = pg |> rvest::html_elements("table.views-table tbody tr")
  if (length(rows) == 0) return(NULL)
  tibble(
    company         = rows |> rvest::html_element("td.views-field-title a") |> rvest::html_text2(),
    detail_path     = rows |> rvest::html_element("td.views-field-title a") |> rvest::html_attr("href"),
    ticker_line     = rows |> rvest::html_element(".ticker-symbol") |> rvest::html_text2(),
    return_1yr_text = rows |> rvest::html_element("td.views-field-field-stock-yearly-return") |> rvest::html_text2(),
    price_text      = rows |> rvest::html_element("td.views-field-field-stock-price") |> rvest::html_text2(),
    as_of           = rows |> rvest::html_element("time") |> rvest::html_attr("datetime"),
    list_page       = p
  )
}

list_file = file.path(raw_dir, "nareit_list_raw.csv")
if (REFRESH || !file.exists(list_file)) {
  pages = list()
  for (p in 0:20) {               # 20 is just a safety cap; it stops at the first empty page
    one = scrape_list_page(p)
    if (is.null(one)) break
    pages[[length(pages) + 1]] = one
  }
  nareit_list = bind_rows(pages)
  readr::write_csv(nareit_list, list_file)
}
nareit_list = readr::read_csv(list_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
nrow(nareit_list)
head(nareit_list)
```

Each REIT also has its own profile page with returns over several horizons, dividend
yield, exchange, and headquarters address. We visit every profile page and keep every
labeled field in long format (one row = one field on one REIT's page). It gets reshaped in `02_clean`.

```{r nareit-detail}
scrape_detail = function(path) {
  Sys.sleep(1)
  pg = rvest::read_html(paste0(base_url, path))
  above  = pg |> rvest::html_elements("div.field.field--label-above, div.field.field--label-inline")   # returns are "inline", dividends are "above"
  inline = pg |> rvest::html_elements("div.field.element-label-inline")
  bind_rows(
    tibble(label = above  |> rvest::html_element(".field__label") |> rvest::html_text2(),
           value = above  |> rvest::html_element(".field__item")  |> rvest::html_text2()),
    tibble(label = inline |> rvest::html_element(".field-label")  |> rvest::html_text2(),
           value = inline |> rvest::html_element(".field-item")   |> rvest::html_text2())
  ) |>
    mutate(detail_path = path)
}

detail_file = file.path(raw_dir, "nareit_detail_raw.csv")
# re-scrape if the saved file is missing the return fields (an earlier version of this code skipped them)
if (REFRESH || !file.exists(detail_file) ||
    !any(grepl("Total Return", readr::read_csv(detail_file, show_col_types = FALSE)$label))) {
  nareit_detail = purrr::map_dfr(nareit_list$detail_path, scrape_detail)
  readr::write_csv(nareit_detail, detail_file)
}
nareit_detail = readr::read_csv(detail_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
nareit_detail |> count(label, sort = TRUE)
```

The ticker is the first piece of text like `KIM | Jericho, New York | Retail`. We need it now to match each REIT to the SEC and Yahoo Finance.

```{r tickers}
reit_tickers = nareit_list |>
  mutate(ticker = stringr::str_trim(stringr::str_extract(ticker_line, "^[^|]+"))) |>
  distinct(ticker) |>
  pull(ticker)
reit_tickers
```

## Source 2: SEC EDGAR (API)

The SEC has free JSON APIs. Every request has to send a User-Agent (from `.Renviron`) and
the SEC asks for no more than 10 requests per second, so we throttle to 5.

```{r sec-helper}
sec_get = function(url) {
  httr2::request(url) |>
    httr2::req_user_agent(Sys.getenv("SEC_USER_AGENT")) |>
    httr2::req_throttle(rate = 5) |>
    # the SEC sometimes answers "busy" (503) or "slow down" (429/403); wait and try again
    httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 5,
                     is_transient = \(resp) httr2::resp_status(resp) %in% c(403, 429, 500, 502, 503),
                     backoff = \(i) 2^i) |>
    httr2::req_perform()
}
```

### 2a. Ticker to CIK lookup

The SEC identifies companies by CIK number, not ticker. `company_tickers.json` maps one to the other.
What one row is: one ticker listed with the SEC.

```{r sec-tickers}
tick_file = file.path(raw_dir, "sec_company_tickers.csv")
if (REFRESH || !file.exists(tick_file)) {
  sec_tickers = sec_get("https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json") |>
    httr2::resp_body_string() |>
    jsonlite::fromJSON() |>
    bind_rows()
  readr::write_csv(sec_tickers, tick_file)
}
sec_tickers = readr::read_csv(tick_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

reits = tibble(ticker = reit_tickers) |>
  left_join(sec_tickers, by = "ticker")

reits |> filter(is.na(cik_str))   # any ticker the SEC does not know (should be none)
reits = reits |> filter(!is.na(cik_str))
```

### 2b. XBRL financial statement facts

`companyfacts` returns every number the company has tagged in its 10-Q and 10-K filings.
We keep a few tags. REITs do not all use the same tag for the same thing (for example
Brixmor reports rental income but not `Revenues`), so we pull backups and pick one in `02_clean`.
What one row is: one reported value for one tag for one period from one filing.

```{r sec-facts}
fact_tags = c("Revenues", "OperatingLeaseLeaseIncome",
              "NetIncomeLoss", "NetIncomeLossAvailableToCommonStockholdersBasic", "ProfitLoss",
              "Assets", "Liabilities")

get_facts = function(cik, ticker) {
  j = sec_get(sprintf("https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK%010d.json", as.integer(cik))) |>
    httr2::resp_body_string() |>
    jsonlite::fromJSON()
  gaap = j$facts$`us-gaap`
  purrr::map_dfr(intersect(fact_tags, names(gaap)), function(tg) {
    u  = gaap[[tg]]$units
    df = u[[1]]
    df$tag  = tg
    df$unit = names(u)[1]
    df
  }) |>
    mutate(ticker = ticker, cik = cik)
}

facts_file = file.path(raw_dir, "sec_companyfacts_raw.csv")
if (REFRESH || !file.exists(facts_file)) {
  sec_facts = purrr::map2_dfr(reits$cik_str, reits$ticker, get_facts) |>
    filter(fy >= START_YEAR - 1)
  readr::write_csv(sec_facts, facts_file)
}
sec_facts = readr::read_csv(facts_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
sec_facts |> count(ticker, tag) |> tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = tag, values_from = n)
```

### 2c. Earnings press releases (8-K, Item 2.02)

Every quarter each REIT files an 8-K under Item 2.02 ("Results of Operations") with the
earnings press release attached as Exhibit 99.1. The press release has the numbers investors
actually care about (occupancy, same-property NOI growth, FFO) that are **not** in the XBRL data.

1. `submissions` API: list the company's filings and keep 8-Ks with item 2.02.
2. Filing index page: find the document whose type is `EX-99.1`.
3. Download it and save it as plain text. These text files are the unstructured input for Source 3.

```{r sec-8k-list}
get_8k_list = function(cik, ticker) {
  j = sec_get(sprintf("https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK%010d.json", as.integer(cik))) |>
    httr2::resp_body_string() |>
    jsonlite::fromJSON()
  r = as_tibble(j$filings$recent)
  if (min(r$filingDate) > paste0(START_YEAR, "-01-01")) {
    warning(ticker, ": recent filings list does not reach back to ", START_YEAR)
  }
  r |>
    filter(form == "8-K",
           stringr::str_detect(items, "2\\.02"),
           filingDate >= paste0(START_YEAR, "-01-15")) |>   # Q4 of the prior year is reported in Jan/Feb
    select(accessionNumber, filingDate, reportDate, items, primaryDocument) |>
    mutate(ticker = ticker, cik = cik)
}

find_ex99 = function(cik, accession) {
  acc = stringr::str_remove_all(accession, "-")
  idx = sprintf("https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/%d/%s/%s-index.html",
                as.integer(cik), acc, accession)
  rows = sec_get(idx) |> httr2::resp_body_string() |> rvest::read_html() |>
    rvest::html_elements("table.tableFile tr")
  docs = tibble(
    type = rows |> rvest::html_element("td:nth-child(4)") |> rvest::html_text2(),
    href = rows |> rvest::html_element("td:nth-child(3) a") |> rvest::html_attr("href")
  ) |>
    filter(type == "EX-99.1")
  if (nrow(docs) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  paste0("https://www.sec.gov", stringr::str_remove(docs$href[1], "^/ix\\?doc="))
}

# If one filing page fails, record the error and keep going instead of stopping the knit.
safe_find_ex99 = function(cik, accession) {
  tryCatch(find_ex99(cik, accession),
           error = function(e) {
             message("Could not read filing ", accession, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
             "ERROR"
           })
}

pr_index_file = file.path(raw_dir, "press_release_index.csv")
if (REFRESH || !file.exists(pr_index_file)) {
  filings = purrr::map2_dfr(reits$cik_str, reits$ticker, get_8k_list)
  filings$ex99_url = "ERROR"
  filings$file = file.path(pr_dir, paste0(filings$ticker, "_", filings$accessionNumber, ".txt"))
  readr::write_csv(filings, pr_index_file)
}
pr_index = readr::read_csv(pr_index_file, show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c"))

# look up (or re-try) every filing whose Exhibit 99.1 link we do not have yet,
# saving progress every 25 filings so a failure part way through is not lost
retry = which(pr_index$ex99_url %in% "ERROR")
for (k in split(retry, ceiling(seq_along(retry) / 25))) {
  pr_index$ex99_url[k] = purrr::map2_chr(pr_index$cik[k], pr_index$accessionNumber[k], safe_find_ex99)
  readr::write_csv(pr_index, pr_index_file)
}
pr_index = pr_index |> mutate(ex99_url = na_if(ex99_url, "NA"))
pr_index |> count(ticker)
pr_index |> filter(is.na(ex99_url))          # 8-Ks with no Exhibit 99.1
pr_index |> filter(ex99_url %in% "ERROR")   # filing pages that failed; knit again to retry them
```

```{r sec-8k-download}
to_get = pr_index |> filter(!is.na(ex99_url), ex99_url != "ERROR", REFRESH | !file.exists(file))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(to_get))) {
  txt = tryCatch(
    sec_get(to_get$ex99_url[i]) |>
      httr2::resp_body_raw() |>      # raw bytes: older SEC files are not always UTF-8
      rvest::read_html() |>
      rvest::html_text2(),
    error = function(e) { message("Download failed: ", to_get$ex99_url[i]); NULL })
  if (!is.null(txt)) writeLines(txt, to_get$file[i], useBytes = TRUE)
}
length(list.files(pr_dir, pattern = "\\.txt$"))
```

## Source 3: Press release metrics (LLM structured extraction)

Each press release is several pages of text and tables, and every REIT words things a bit
differently ("leased occupancy", "same center NOI", "Nareit FFO"). We send the first 15,000
characters of each one (the headline section where these numbers live) to `gpt-5.6-luna`
through `ellmer` and ask for the same fields back every time.

What one row is: one earnings press release (one REIT, one quarter).

```{r llm-schema}
pr_type = ellmer::type_object(
  period_year    = ellmer::type_integer("Calendar year of the quarter whose results are reported, e.g. 2026"),
  period_quarter = ellmer::type_integer("Quarter (1-4) whose results are reported. A fourth-quarter / full-year release is 4"),
  property_focus = ellmer::type_enum(
    values = c("grocery_anchored_center", "open_air_center", "mall_outlet", "net_lease", "mixed"),
    description = "Main property type the company owns, based on how it describes itself"),
  occupancy_pct = ellmer::type_number(
    "Headline total portfolio occupancy or leased rate for the quarter in percent, e.g. 96.6. Use the total (or pro-rata) portfolio number, not small-shop or anchor only. Leave empty if not stated", required = FALSE),
  same_property_noi_growth_pct = ellmer::type_number(
    "Year-over-year same property / same center / comparable NOI growth for the quarter in percent, e.g. 4.9 (negative if it fell). Quarter, not year-to-date. Leave empty if not stated", required = FALSE),
  ffo_per_share = ellmer::type_number(
    "Nareit-defined FFO per diluted share for the quarter in dollars (not Core, Normalized, or AFFO). Leave empty if not stated", required = FALSE),
  core_ffo_per_share = ellmer::type_number(
    "Core FFO, Normalized FFO, Operating FFO, or AFFO per diluted share for the quarter in dollars, if reported", required = FALSE),
  rent_spread_pct = ellmer::type_number(
    "Blended (all comparable leases) cash rent spread or rent recapture rate change for the quarter, in percent. For a recapture rate of 103.5% report 3.5. Leave empty if not stated", required = FALSE),
  guidance_change = ellmer::type_enum(
    values = c("raised", "maintained", "lowered", "initiated", "not_mentioned"),
    description = "What the release says about full-year guidance / outlook compared with the last update"),
  net_debt_to_ebitda = ellmer::type_number(
    "Net debt to EBITDA (or EBITDAre) ratio, e.g. 5.4. Leave empty if not stated", required = FALSE)
)
```

The extraction runs in batches of 25 and appends to a CSV as it goes, so if a call fails
or you stop halfway, the next knit only sends the press releases that are not done yet.

```{r llm-extract}
llm_file = file.path(raw_dir, "llm_press_release_extract.csv")
done = if (file.exists(llm_file) && !REFRESH) readr::read_csv(llm_file, show_col_types = FALSE)$file else character(0)

todo = pr_index |>
  filter(file.exists(file), !file %in% done)

chat = ellmer::chat_openai(
  model  = "gpt-5.6-luna",
  params = ellmer::params(reasoning_effort = "none"),
  system_prompt = paste(
    "You read quarterly earnings press releases from U.S. retail REITs and pull out numbers.",
    "Only report a number if it is written in the text. Never calculate or guess a value.",
    "Percentages are plain numbers (96.6 not 0.966).")
)

batches = split(seq_len(nrow(todo)), ceiling(seq_len(nrow(todo)) / 25))
for (b in batches) {
  prompts = purrr::map(b, function(i) {
    txt = paste(readLines(todo$file[i], warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
    paste0("Company ticker: ", todo$ticker[i], "\nFiled: ", todo$filingDate[i], "\n\n",
           substr(txt, 1, 15000))
  })
  res = tryCatch(
    ellmer::parallel_chat_structured(chat, prompts, type = pr_type),
    error = function(e) { message("Batch failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL }
  )
  if (is.null(res)) next
  res$file = todo$file[b]
  readr::write_csv(res, llm_file, append = file.exists(llm_file))
}

llm_raw = readr::read_csv(llm_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
nrow(llm_raw)
head(llm_raw)
```

## Source 4: FRED 10-year Treasury yield (API)

REITs are often treated as "bond proxies", so the 10-year Treasury yield (`DGS10`) is the
rate we compare against. What one row is: one trading day.

```{r fred}
fred_file = file.path(raw_dir, "fred_dgs10_raw.csv")
if (REFRESH || !file.exists(fred_file)) {
  fred = httr2::request("https://api.stlouisfed.org/fred/series/observations") |>
    httr2::req_url_query(
      series_id         = "DGS10",
      api_key           = Sys.getenv("FRED_API_KEY"),
      file_type         = "json",
      observation_start = paste0(START_YEAR - 1, "-10-01")
    ) |>
    httr2::req_perform() |>
    httr2::resp_body_string() |>
    jsonlite::fromJSON()
  readr::write_csv(fred$observations |> select(date, value), fred_file)
}
dgs10_raw = readr::read_csv(fred_file, show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = "cc")
tail(dgs10_raw)
```

## Source 5: Daily stock prices (Yahoo Finance chart API)

We call Yahoo Finance's chart API directly with `httr2` (the same data `tidyquant` uses, but
calling it ourselves is more reliable). `adjusted` is the closing price adjusted for dividends
and splits, so the change in it is close to a total return. What one row is: one ticker on one trading day.

```{r prices}
to_num = function(x) vapply(x, function(v) if (is.null(v)) NA_real_ else as.numeric(v), numeric(1))  # null -> NA

get_prices = function(tk) {
  Sys.sleep(0.5)
  j = httr2::request(paste0("https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/", tk)) |>
    httr2::req_url_query(
      period1  = as.integer(as.POSIXct(paste0(START_YEAR - 1, "-12-01"), tz = "UTC")),
      period2  = as.integer(Sys.time()),
      interval = "1d"
    ) |>
    httr2::req_user_agent("Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)") |>   # Yahoo blocks requests with no browser name
    httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 3) |>
    httr2::req_perform() |>
    httr2::resp_body_string() |>
    jsonlite::fromJSON(simplifyVector = FALSE)
  r = j$chart$result[[1]]
  q = r$indicators$quote[[1]]
  tibble(symbol   = tk,
         date     = as.Date(as.POSIXct(to_num(r$timestamp), origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "America/New_York")),
         open     = to_num(q$open),  high = to_num(q$high), low = to_num(q$low),
         close    = to_num(q$close), volume = to_num(q$volume),
         adjusted = to_num(r$indicators$adjclose[[1]]$adjclose))
}

safe_get_prices = function(tk) {
  tryCatch(get_prices(tk), error = function(e) { message("Prices failed for ", tk, ": ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
}

price_file = file.path(raw_dir, "yahoo_prices_raw.csv")
if (REFRESH || !file.exists(price_file)) {
  prices = purrr::map_dfr(reits$ticker, safe_get_prices)
  readr::write_csv(prices, price_file)
}
prices_raw = readr::read_csv(price_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
setdiff(reits$ticker, prices_raw$symbol)   # tickers with no prices (should be empty)
prices_raw |> group_by(symbol) |> summarise(first = min(date), last = max(date), n = n())
```

Everything above is already written to `../data/raw/`:

```{r raw-files}
list.files(raw_dir)
```
